taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy for **grid-based logic games** (puzzle types), with each of your listed games placed into the most fitting category. (Many puzzles could fit multiple categories; I’m choosing the primary “core mechanic”.)

---

## 1) Illumination / Visibility (line-of-sight constraints)
- **Akari** (light bulbs illuminate rows/columns; avoid bulb-to-bulb illumination)
- **Kurodoko** (numbers count visible white cells until black/edge)
- **Kurotto** (numbers constrain contiguous black runs in row/column)

---

## 2) Loop / Path Drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
### 2A) Generic single-loop / cycle puzzles
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Masyu** (loop with turn/straight requirements at circles)
- **Nagareru** (loop with direction/wind constraints)
- **Moon-or-Sun** (loop visits rooms; moon/sun per room)
- **Suraromu** (loop must pass gates; start/end at open circle)
- **Slitherlink** (loop edges constrained by surrounding numbers)
- **Yajilin** (loop avoids numbered/black cells; arrow direction counts black cells)

### 2B) Loop with “room visitation” / region interaction
- **Moon-or-Sun** (room-by-room moon/sun rule)
- **Suraromu** (gates are special edges; loop passes each gate once)

---

## 3) Region Partitioning / Tiling (rectangles/blocks/rooms)
### 3A) Rectangle/area tiling with numbers
- **Shikaku** (rectangles determined by numbers)
- **Tilepaint** (tiles outlined by bold lines; numbers constrain black counts along diagonals)
- **Nurimeizu** (rooms form a maze; S→G through white cells)
- **Ripple Effect** (rooms contain consecutive numbers)

### 3B) Polyomino / shape placement in regions
- **Evolomino** (fill blocks with same number; block-size/adjacency constraints)
- **LITS** (place tetrominoes in bold regions; connectivity + no large squares)
- **Sashigane** (L-shaped blocks; circles/arrows mark knee/end and size)

### 3C) Block-structure puzzles (non-rectangular blocks)
- **Chained Block** (blocks of black cells; chain of unique shapes/sizes)
- **Double Choco** (pair of same-form areas in each solid-line block; counts per color)
- **Five Cells** (partition into blocks of exactly 5 cells; frame-inclusive perimeter counts)
- **Fillomino** (fill each block with its number; same-number blocks cannot touch)
- **Hashiwokakero** (bridges between islands; implicitly region-like connectivity)

---

## 4) Coloring / Shading (black/white cell constraints)
### 4A) “No adjacency / connectivity” coloring
- **Hitori** (duplicate numbers forbidden; black cells not touching; whites connected)
- **Heyawake** (painted cells per room count; white connectivity + separation rules)
- **Nurikabe** (black wall connectivity; numbered white regions)
- **Nuritwin** (two blocks per region; shaded connectivity across boundaries; no 2×2 all shaded)
- **Usowan** (colored cells with number-adjacency; numbers cannot be colored)
- **Shakashaka** (place black triangles; uncovered area must be rectangle/square)

### 4B) “Rectangle/square formation” constraints
- **Choco Banana** (black cells form rectangles/squares; white cells must not)

### 4C) “Wrong number” / local consistency
- **Makaro** (rooms contain numbers up to N; arrow points to max around it; no same number adjacent across rooms)

---

## 5) Number-Run / Sequence Constraints (non-loop, line-based)
- **Juosan** (each cell is — or |; territories count additional marks; max run lengths)
- **Nansuke** (fill with digits from list; orientation-based placement)
- **Hebi** (snakes numbered 1→5 sequentially; directional “attack” constraints)
- **Pencils** (pencil tips with lengths; lines through cells; no self-cross/branch)
- **Satogaeri** (move circles within countries; each country ends with exactly one circle; pass-through counts)

---

## 6) Pair Connection / Non-crossing Paths (connect matching endpoints)
- **Numberlink** (connect equal numbers with non-crossing continuous lines)

---

## 7) Bridge / Network Construction (graph-like edges)
- **Hashiwokakero** (islands connected by 1–2 bridges; all islands linked)

---

## 8) Sudoku / Latin-structure Grids (row/column/block number placement)
- **Sudoku** (standard 1–9 in rows/columns/3×3 blocks)

---

## 9) “Arrow / Directional Flow” / Movement Puzzles
- **Nagareru** (wind direction affects loop movement)
- **Satogaeri** (circles move through cells; arrows not present but movement is directional)
- **Yosenabe** (move circles into gray areas; arrows show straight movement; sum constraints)

---
